question:
By Interchanging the given two numbers which of the following equation will be not correct?

9 and 3

I. 7 × 4 ÷ 2 - 9 + 3 = 22

II. 9 + 4 - 6 × 3 ÷ 2 = -10
solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4671232025562bc3ba9a781319d633acf8cd8e78dc8e96912cd7564a7df4717d.png] 

I. Given equation : 7 × 4 ÷ 2 - 9 + 3 = 22

After interchanging the given two numbers 9 and 3 the equation is as follows : 7 × 4 ÷ 2 - 3 + 9 = 22

⇒ 7 × __**4 ÷ 2**__ - 3 + 9 = 22

⇒ __**7 × 2**__ - 3 + 9 = 22

⇒ __**14**__ - 3 __**+ 9**__ = 22

⇒ __**23**____** - 3**__ = 22

⇒ 20 ≠ 22

LHS ≠ RHS

II. Given equation : 9 + 4 - 6 × 3 ÷ 2 = -10

After interchanging the given two numbers 9 and 3 the equation is as follows : 3 + 4 - 6 × 9 ÷ 2 = -10

⇒ 3 + 4 - 6 × __**9 ÷ 2**__ = -10

⇒ 3 + 4 - __**6 × 4.5**__ = -10

⇒ __**3 + 4**__ - 27 = -10

⇒ __**7 - 27**__ = -10

⇒ -20 ≠ -10

LHS ≠ RHS

∴ Here, Both equations I and II are not correct.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Both I and II".**
